title: HAZEM RADHOUANI
description: Architect with international experience: project work in Tunisia, France and Morocco, and research experience in Japan.

cover.alt: Black and white photograph of an earthen alley between rubble walls, with two lit doorways, in a ruined village

manifesto.text: A village in the Tunisian Jérid region | raw earth architecture never previously documented. Multiple on-site survey campaigns conducted: measurements, documentary photography, interviews with former inhabitants.

flagship.title: Al-Arg
flagship.line: The ruined village that founded the conviction.
flagship.text: The thesis operates at three scales simultaneously: a territorial analysis of the conditions that produced the abandonment, an urban proposal for the reactivation of the village as a place of memory, culture, and temporary dwelling, and an architectural intervention on a key building within the fabric.

hero.alt: Aerial render of Al-Arg at sunset: earth-walled buildings, roof terraces and open courtyards below a grove of date palms, in deep orange light

scales.label: Territorial
scales.caption: Site map | Al-Arg within the Jérid. Reading of the oasis territory as a system | water, road, inhabited fabric.
scales.alt: Coloured map of the oasis territory around Al-Arg: palm groves in three greens, residential, saline and unplanted areas, roads and routes towards the neighbouring oases and towns

scales.label: Urban
scales.caption: Site plan | rehabilitation proposal.
scales.alt: Site plan of the Al-Arg rehabilitation proposal

scales.label: Architectural
scales.caption: Ground floor plan | proposed
scales.alt: Coloured plan of the rehabilitated building: black earth walls around several courtyards, small planted patios and pale blue rooms among the surrounding houses
